title: Potassium Deficiency in Crops
content:
Potassium (K) is a macronutrient critical for disease resistance, water regulation, and grain quality. Potassium deficiency is widespread in Indian soils, particularly in Bihar, Eastern UP, and Odisha.

Symptoms: Yellowing/browning starting at leaf tips and margins (tip burn), moving inward. Lower/older leaves affected first. Weak stems, increased lodging. Reduced grain size and quality. Increased susceptibility to fungal and bacterial diseases.

Causes: Sandy/light soils (low K holding capacity). Continuous cropping without K fertilization. Excessive N application (antagonistic effect). Heavy rainfall leaching K from root zone.

Management: Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP) at 40-60 kg K2O/ha based on soil test. Alternatively, use vermicompost or crop residue incorporation. For organic: wood ash, compost, or Sulphate of Potash (SOP) for chloride-sensitive crops.
content_hi:
पोटाश एक प्रमुख पोषक तत्व है जो रोग प्रतिरोधक क्षमता, जल नियंत्रण और दाने की गुणवत्ता के लिए आवश्यक है।

लक्षण: पत्तियों के किनारे और सिरे पीले/भूरे होना। निचली पत्तियां पहले प्रभावित। कमजोर तने। दाने छोटे।

प्रबंधन: मिट्टी परीक्षण के अनुसार पोटाश (MOP) 40-60 किलो/हेक्टेयर डालें।
summary: Potassium deficiency causes leaf tip burn, weak stems, and increases disease susceptibility. Apply MOP based on soil test.
summary_hi: पोटाश की कमी से पत्तियों के किनारे जलते हैं, तने कमजोर होते हैं और रोग अधिक लगते हैं। मिट्टी परीक्षण करवाएं।
actions: Get soil tested for potassium (K) levels at nearest KVK or Soil Testing Lab.
Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP) at 40-60 kg/ha if soil test shows K deficiency.
Incorporate crop residues (paddy straw, wheat straw) into soil after harvest — they contain significant potassium.
Apply vermicompost at 2-3 tonnes/ha to improve overall soil potassium status.
Avoid applying excess nitrogen when potassium is deficient — the imbalance worsens disease susceptibility.
warnings: Do NOT apply MOP to tobacco, potato, or grapes if chloride sensitivity is a concern. Use Sulphate of Potash (SOP) instead.
Potassium deficiency symptoms mimic nitrogen deficiency in early stages. Check: K deficiency starts at leaf tips/margins, N deficiency causes uniform yellowing from tip.
